coverage.remaining: None. The whole document was read, including the recommendation chapters, the implementation matrix, the acknowledgments and the photo credits.
coverage.note: This is a policy document, not a survey, and it is the first document on the SF Planning historic-context-statements page that carries no address-level facts at all. It is organised as three goals — well-being, culture, opportunity — broken into recommended actions, each with benefits, challenges and first steps, and closes with an implementation matrix of responsible agencies and timeframes. It names cultural districts (Compton's Transgender, Leather and LGBTQ, Castro, Calle 24), institutions (the GLBT Historical Society and Museum, the LGBT Center, the Youth Navigation Center) and public-realm projects (Eagle Plaza, Ringold Alley), but it locates none of them by street number: the museum recommendation goes as far as "possible site locations in SoMa or Castro". The whole document contains exactly one numbered street address, 625 Polk Street, and it appears in a photograph credit for a Tavern Guild ball at California Hall — a building whose page already carries that history from the 2015 LGBTQ context statement and the city's landmark record, so it adds nothing. Neighbouring documents on the same SF Planning page are where this subject's addresses live: the 2015 Citywide Historic Context Statement for LGBTQ History (mined as lgbtq-hcs) and the 2004 sexual-identity subcultures statement (mined as sexual-identity-subcultures). The strategy is closed out; nothing in it is outstanding.
